title: Choose the visual world for EV Readiness Check
question: The roll assigned Trailhead Sign. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Trailhead Sign
options.lineage: Forest Service routed-wood trailhead signs and trail difficulty markers
options.thesis: Your EV readiness, posted like the sign at the trailhead: how hard this trail is for you, and how far to each thing that matters.
options.viewport: A cedar-brown top rail; the verdict as a routed trailhead sign with its difficulty marker and a mileage stack (nearest fast charger 3.9 mi, range you need 45 mi, Rocky Mountain NP 36 mi); reasons and cards on a pale lichen ground; Get my EV plan as the primary button.
options.risk: Difficulty symbols come from ski areas; set timidly they read as decoration, set loudly 'Not yet' could feel like a judgment instead of terrain.

raised.raise: State by form, not hue: every verdict and reason carries its shape and a word, so color is never the only signal.
Keyed apparatus: each number carries a small source key that opens its assumption, so the work is shown beside the claim.
Whole-cell grid: sign panels and cards snap to one 8-column module, never half cells.
Fixed furniture per entry: every charger and park carries the same name plate, distance, and one-line note.
One family, never pure black: Public Sans sets sign, card, and caption; ink is iron, not #000.

options.label: Trip Strip
options.lineage: spiral-bound road-trip strip maps planned for one family's route
options.thesis: Your answer as a personal route strip: from your ZIP, down past every charging stop and check, to the park you drive to.
options.viewport: Verdict as the trip title; a highlighter route runs down the left from 'Home, 80302' through stops (fast charger 3.9 mi, range check 45 mi, fuel cost) to Rocky Mountain NP 36 mi; each stop is a card beside the route.
options.risk: My top-ranked idea and the more familiar road-trip trope; the narrow strip can waste desktop width.

options.label: Ticket Wallet
options.lineage: jet-age airline ticket wallets with carbon coupons
options.thesis: The check as a coupon book: each question is a coupon, skipped answers stamp ASSUMED, and the plan tears off.
options.viewport: Verdict on the top coupon with carbon numerals; assumptions stamped in red; the EV plan as a perforated stub beside it.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and holds product clarity (stamped assumptions are honest); loses audience identification, since air travel is not this visitor's world.
options.risk: Can read as a travel theme rather than a car-and-parks tool.

options.label: Emission-Line Rail
options.lineage: glass spectrograms on a viewing box
options.thesis: State carried by line height, dash, and doubling on a charcoal continuum.
options.viewport: One off-centre rail with the verdict as a doubled bright line.
options.case: Loses both axes: renters planning park trips do not read spectrograms, and line-form state is opaque to a general public.

options.label: Centre-Rail Reference
options.thesis: Dense twin columns with keyed apparatus in the margin.
options.viewport: Two short columns around a rail of vermilion keys.
options.case: Loses both axes: reads as a scholarly book, not a quick tool for a car decision.
options.risk: Too bookish for a phone visitor from a social post.

options.label: Grid Specimen
options.thesis: Letterforms built cell by cell on a visible grid.
options.viewport: The verdict built from grid cells.
options.case: Loses both axes: a type poster, not a readiness answer.

options.label: Character Catalog
options.thesis: A ranked roster of mascots with name plates and notes.
options.viewport: Chargers and parks as a ranked mascot roster.
options.case: Loses both axes: playful mascots undercut an honest money-and-range answer.

options.label: Design Annual Plates
options.thesis: Registration furniture and one grotesque on near-white stock.
options.viewport: Results as numbered plates with crosshair corners.
options.case: Loses both axes: an art-book frame for a practical decision.
options.kept: One family, ink never pure black.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean EV-calculator look, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Verdict card with a green gauge, stat tiles for charging, range, and cost, and a green primary button.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every EV calculator by design.
